## Completion Report

**Questions asked & answered**: 5 of 5. You deferred to my judgement on all five; for the `user@1.2.3.4` question you asked for the safe handling, so I chose full redaction (`[EMAIL]`) over the narrower `user@[IP]` that the original wording implied.

**Updated spec**: `specs/001-redact-log-pii/spec.md`

**Decisions recorded**:
1. **Encoding** — fixed UTF-8 in and out, non-UTF-8 bytes round-tripped as the same bytes, never locale-dependent (new FR-005a, FR-005b)
2. **Output consumer closes early** (`| head`) — quiet stop, empty stderr, no count summary, exit 0 (new FR-028)
3. **`user@1.2.3.4`** — email rule now accepts a dotted-number domain and redacts the whole span including the username; no octet range check in that position, so `user@999.1.1.1` also redacts (FR-007 revised, new FR-007a)
4. **Invalid command line** — usage diagnostic naming the argument, no output, exit 2; reuses status 2 rather than adding a third (new FR-029)
5. **Directory as a FILE argument** — an ordinary read failure on the FR-025 path with no stack trace (FR-025 broadened)

**Sections touched**: Clarifications (new), User Story 1 Acceptance Scenarios, User Story 4 Acceptance Scenarios, Edge Cases, Functional Requirements (Invocation/Text handling, Email addresses, Counting, Exit status and failure reporting), Success Criteria (SC-002, SC-003, SC-006), Assumptions.

**Spec quality checklist**: 16/16 → 16/16 items passing. No newly passing items, no regressions, none left unchecked. I deliberately left the file byte-identical since no checkbox changed state.

| Category | Status |
|---|---|
| Functional Scope & Behavior | Clear |
| Domain & Data Model | Clear |
| Interaction & UX Flow | **Resolved** (early output close, invalid usage) |

**Nothing is deferred with high impact.** One judgement worth your eye before planning: FR-007a makes the email rule swallow numeric-domain addresses whole, which means `user@1.2.3.4` no longer contributes to the `ips` count. If you'd rather see such hosts counted as IPs, say so and I'll flip it.
